title: Absa Fellowship Programme South Africa 2026
fields_of_study: STEM fields (Science [including Health science, but excluding Medical or veterinary studies], Technology, Engineering and Mathematics)
eligibility: You must be a citizen of one of these African countries: South Africa, Mozambique, Zambia, Botswana, Tanzania, Kenya, Mauritius, Seychelles, Uganda or Ghana
You must be between 18 and 25 years old
You must be currently in Matric or have completed Matric
You must be entering your 1st year of undergraduate study in 2026
You must intend on studying towards an undergraduate degree qualification, within one of the fields of study listed above
You must have achieved a minimum overall average of 65% in Matric latest results
You must intend on studying at a public university in South Africa
You must be a leader
closing_date_text: 10 September 2025. (Applications submitted after this date will not be accepted – please apply before the closing date to ensure your application is considered.)
application_instructions: Scholarships will be awarded to 50 students, for studies within the following fields:
Commerce
Humanities and Social Sciences
STEM fields (Science [including Health science, but excluding Medical or veterinary studies], Technology, Engineering and Mathematics)
Creative Arts
Digital / Data Design

The Absa Fellowship Programme is so much more than a regular scholarship or bursary programme. It is a leadership development programme, that provides candidates with financial support towards their studies, as well as the chance to participate in a specially curated leadership development programme created by Absa.
** RELATED BURSARIES **
View our other Arts Bursaries and Scholarships here .
View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here .
View our other Science & Technology Bursaries and Scholarships here .
View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The fellowship will provide cover for the following study related expenses: full tuition fees, textbooks, educational equipment, laptop, accommodation in university residence or private, meal allowance, monthly stipend, monthly data allowance, student medical aid cover.

Recipients will also receive the following benefits: leadership programme, travel if required, learner modules and guides, online lectures and assessments, emotional wellness check-in sessions and academic tutoring and mentoring.
Candidates will be shortlisted based on the score achieved in the psychometric assessment. Shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview.
www.zabursaries.co.za is committed to keeping you up to date with the latest bursary opportunities, and this article covers all details about the Absa Fellowship.

Data Scientists are individuals with advance training in Mathematics and Computer Science, with expertise in data mining and information management. Data Scientists are vital to businesses as they aid in mitigating risk and fraud; they aid businesses in seeing what products and services are selling the most, and they aid in personalising customer’s experiences by helping the sales and marketing team in understanding their target audience.

Data Scientists work both in the field of technology and social science, finding the latest trends to manage data. Data Scientists make sense of all data collected from social media feeds, smart devices, emails, etc. and compile them into a structured database.
It is essential for a Data Scientist to have excellent communication skills as well as be data-driven, analytical thinkers, leaders, and highly organised.
